note: Distance from 0, so never negative.
A positive integer above 1 that is not prime.
ex: 9 is composite because 9 = 3 × 3.

note: Each is 2 more than the previous one.
ex: 6, 8, 10 are consecutive even integers.

note: Each is 1 more than the previous one: n, n+1, n+2.
ex: 14, 15 and 16 are consecutive integers.

note: The bottom number.
ex: In 3/4, the denominator is 4.

note: A number has digits; 'digit' is never a number above 9.
ex: The number 507 has three digits: 5, 0 and 7.

note: No two values are equal.
ex: a, b and c are distinct, so a ≠ b.

note: 'a is divisible by b' means a/b is an integer.
ex: 45 is divisible by 9 because 45/9 = 5.
5 is a divisor of 35.

note: Zero is even. Negative numbers can be even.
ex: -4, 0 and 18 are even.

note: Same as divisor when talking about integers.
ex: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.

note: Also called greatest common factor (GCF).
ex: The GCD of 18 and 24 is 6.

note: Second digit after the decimal point.
ex: In 2.738, the hundredths digit is 3.

note: Includes negatives and zero: ..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ...
ex: -4, 0 and 9 are integers; 2.5 is not.
√2 and π are irrational.
The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12.

note: Multiples of n are n, 2n, 3n, ... (0 is also a multiple).
ex: 24 is a multiple of 6.

note: Includes zero, unlike 'positive'.
ex: If x is nonnegative, x could be 0.

note: The top number.
ex: In 3/4, the numerator is 3.
7 and -3 are odd.

note: The square of an integer.
ex: 49 is a perfect square because 49 = 7².

note: Zero is not positive.
ex: 1, 2, 3, ... are positive integers.

vi: phân tích ra thừa số nguyên tố

note: 2 is the only even prime; 1 is not prime.
ex: The first five primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11.

note: Can be written as a fraction of integers.
ex: 0.75 = 3/4 is rational.

note: On the GMAT, assume all numbers are real.
ex: -3, 0.5 and √5 are real numbers.

note: The reciprocal of x is 1/x; 0 has no reciprocal.
ex: The reciprocal of 2/5 is 5/2.
The tens digit of 3,486 is 8.

note: First digit after the decimal point.
ex: In 2.738, the tenths digit is 7.

note: Ends after finitely many digits.
ex: 1/8 = 0.125 terminates; 1/3 does not.

note: Also called the ones digit.
ex: The units digit of 3,486 is 6.

note: Usually means nonnegative integers; do not confuse with 'integer'.
ex: 0, 1 and 12 are whole numbers.
In 2⁵, the base is 2.

note: Order matters: 'the difference between a and b' is usually a - b.
ex: The difference between 10 and 3 is 7.
In 17 ÷ 5, the dividend is 17.

note: Implies no remainder.
ex: 24 cookies evenly divided among 6 children gives 4 each.

note: Also called power.
ex: In 2⁵, the exponent is 5.

vi: thứ tự thực hiện phép tính
note: Parentheses, exponents, then × and ÷, then + and -.
'x to the third power' means x³.
ex: 2 to the fourth power is 16.

note: Result of multiplication.
ex: The product of 4 and 9 is 36.

note: Result of division (in integer division, the whole-number part).
ex: When 17 is divided by 5, the quotient is 3.

note: Always 0 ≤ remainder < divisor.
ex: When 17 is divided by 5, the remainder is 2.

vi: làm tròn đến hàng gần nhất
ex: 3.46 rounded to the nearest tenth is 3.5.

note: √ always means the nonnegative root.
Result of addition.
ex: The sum of 4 and 9 is 13.
In 5x², the coefficient is 5.

note: Coordinate geometry is tested as part of algebra.
ex: The point (3, -2) lies in the coordinate plane.
x² - 9 factors as (x - 3)(x + 3).
If f(x) = x² + 1, then f(3) = 10.

note: 'y in terms of x' means y = (something with x).
ex: If 2y = x + 6, then y in terms of x is (x + 6)/2.

vi: bất phương trình, bất đẳng thức
note: Flip the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative.
ex: -2x > 6 gives x < -3.
y = 3x - 1 is a linear equation.
x² - 5x + 6 = 0 is a quadratic equation.
If 2 < x < 5, x lies in a range of values.

note: A value that makes the equation true; also called solution.
ex: The roots of x² - 5x + 6 = 0 are 2 and 3.
In the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, each term is 4 more than the last.

note: Rise over run.
ex: The line y = 2x + 5 has slope 2.
Solve 2x + 1 = 9 for x: x = 4.
x + y = 10 and x - y = 2 form a system.

note: The y-value where the line crosses the y-axis.
ex: y = 2x + 5 has y-intercept 5.
There are 6 arrangements of the letters A, B, C.

note: Each option is equally likely.
ex: A card is chosen at random from 10 cards.
Average = sum ÷ number of values.

note: Order does not matter.
ex: Choosing 2 of 4 people: 6 combinations.

note: P(not A) = 1 - P(A).
ex: P(at least one head in 2 flips) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4.

note: How many times a value occurs.
ex: In 1, 3, 3, 3, the value 3 has frequency 3.

note: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
ex: Two separate coin flips are independent.

note: Same as arithmetic mean or average.
ex: The mean of 2, 4 and 9 is 5.

note: Sort the values first; with an even count, average the middle two.
ex: The median of 3, 8, 1, 6 is (3 + 6)/2 = 4.5.

vi: mốt (giá trị xuất hiện nhiều nhất)
note: A list can have more than one mode.
ex: The mode of 2, 5, 5, 7 is 5.

vi: xung khắc (không thể cùng xảy ra)
note: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B). Not the same as independent.
ex: Rolling a 2 and rolling a 5 on one roll are mutually exclusive.

note: Total = A + B - Both + Neither.
ex: 20 study French, 15 Spanish, 5 both: 30 study at least one.

note: Order matters.
ex: Arranging 3 books on a shelf: 3! = 6 permutations.

note: Favourable outcomes ÷ total equally likely outcomes.
ex: The probability of rolling a 6 on a fair die is 1/6.

note: Largest value minus smallest value.
ex: The range of 4, 9, 15 is 11.

note: Measures spread around the mean; adding a constant to every value does not change it.
ex: The list 5, 5, 5 has standard deviation 0.
Two overlapping circles show students in French, Spanish or both.

note: Each value counts in proportion to its weight.
ex: 3 tests at 80 and 1 test at 60 average 75.
Draw a ball, put it back, then draw again.

note: The total shrinks after each draw.
ex: Draw 2 balls from 5 without replacement: 5 then 4 choices.

note: ≥, includes the number.
ex: At least 3 means 3, 4, 5, ...

note: ≤, includes the number.
ex: At most 3 means 3 or fewer.

note: Total distance ÷ total time, not the average of speeds.
ex: 60 miles at 30 mph then 60 miles at 60 mph: average 40 mph.
5% commission on $2,000 of sales is $100.
100 decreased by 25 percent is 75.

note: Strict >.
ex: Sales exceed 1,000 units: sales > 1,000.

note: Strict <, used for countable things.
ex: Fewer than 5 errors: 0 to 4 errors.

note: Asks for a difference, not a total.
ex: A has 12, B has 8: A has 4 more.
The integers from 4 to 9, inclusive, number 6.

note: Tells you the amount of change.
ex: Price 50 increased by 10 becomes 60.

note: Tells you the final value.
ex: Price 50 increased to 60: the change is 10.

note: Compound interest earns interest on interest.
ex: $1,000 at 10% compound for 2 years becomes $1,210.

note: Order flips: '3 less than x' is x - 3, not 3 - x.
ex: 3 less than y is y - 3.

vi: phần tăng giá (so với giá vốn)
note: Usually a percent of cost.
ex: A 25% markup on a $40 cost gives $50.
Mix 2 liters of 10% salt water with 3 liters of 20% salt water.

note: Strict >. Watch the order: '5 more than x' is x + 5.
ex: 5 more than twice x is 2x + 5.

note: Same as at least (≥).
ex: No less than 10 hours: hours ≥ 10.

note: Same as at most (≤).
ex: No more than 40 guests: guests ≤ 40.
60 miles per hour: 60 miles in each hour.

note: (new - old) ÷ old × 100.
ex: From 80 to 100 is a 25 percent change.

vi: lớn hơn bao nhiêu phần trăm
note: Compare to the smaller (original) value.
ex: 60 is 20 percent greater than 50.

vi: nhỏ hơn bao nhiêu phần trăm
note: Compare to the original value, not the new one.
ex: 40 is 20 percent less than 50.

note: 'Of' means multiply.
ex: 20 percent of 50 is 0.2 × 50 = 10.

note: A difference between two percents, not a percent change.
ex: From 10% to 12% is 2 percentage points but a 20 percent increase.

note: Revenue minus cost.
ex: Sell for $120, cost $90: profit is $30.

note: An equation stating two ratios are equal; also 'share of a whole'.
ex: 2/5 = x/20 gives x = 8.

vi: tốc độ, tỉ lệ (theo đơn vị thời gian)
note: Distance = rate × time; work = rate × time.
ex: At a rate of 5 pages per minute, 20 pages take 4 minutes.

note: A ratio gives relative size, not actual amounts.
ex: Boys to girls is 2:3; with 10 boys there are 15 girls.

note: Match items in the same order they are listed.
ex: A and B earn 30 and $40, respectively: A earns 30.

note: Add rates, not times.
ex: One pipe fills a tank in 3 h, another in 6 h: together 2 h.

note: If (1) is sufficient the answer is A or D; if not, it is B, C or E.
ex: (1) fails, (2) works alone: the answer is B.
If the answer is always yes, the statement is sufficient.

note: Two or more possible answers remain.
ex: x² = 9 is not sufficient to find x: x could be 3 or -3.

note: Simplify the question before reading the statements.
ex: 'Is 2x > 10?' rephrases to 'Is x > 5?'.

note: Statements are always true; never doubt them.
ex: Statement (1): x is a prime number.

note: Enough information to answer with ONE value or a definite yes/no.
ex: If you can find exactly one value of x, the statement is sufficient.

note: Each statement is first tested without the other.
ex: (1) alone is sufficient if it fixes the answer by itself.

note: Plug in different numbers to find two different answers.
ex: Try x = 2 and x = -2 to show 'Is x > 0?' is not answered.

note: Only tested after both fail alone (choices C or E).
ex: Together, x + y = 7 and x - y = 1 give x = 4.

note: Sufficient only if one single value results.
ex: What is the value of y?

note: A definite 'always no' is also sufficient.
ex: Is n odd? If n must be even, the answer is a definite no: sufficient.

note: A common way to weaken a causal argument.
ex: Maybe the weather, not the ad, raised sales.

note: Premises + conclusion.
ex: Sales rose after the ad; so the ad caused the rise.

note: An unstated premise the argument needs.
ex: The plan assumes residents will actually use the new bridge.

note: Asks what role each bold part plays.
ex: The first bold part is a claim the argument opposes.
New data bolster the claim that the drug works.
The argument makes a causal claim: X causes Y.

note: The main claim the author wants you to accept.
ex: Therefore, the city should build a second bridge.

note: Two things moving together; not proof of cause.
ex: Ice cream sales and swimming accidents both rise in summer.

note: A point against the conclusion that the author acknowledges.
ex: Although costs are high, the plan is worth it.

note: Two facts that seem to conflict; find what explains both.
ex: Sales rose, yet profits fell.

note: Find the question whose answer would most affect the argument.
ex: Which would be most useful to know in evaluating the argument?
The argument confuses correlation with causation: that is the flaw.

note: Treat every answer choice as true; judge only its effect.
ex: Which of the following, if true, ...

note: Must be true from the facts given; no outside ideas.
ex: All A are B; x is A; so x is B.

vi: hợp lý, có khả năng đúng
ex: A plausible explanation is that costs rose.

note: Facts given in support; accept them as true.
ex: Premise: sales rose 10 percent after the campaign.

vi: suy ra một cách hợp lý
note: Inference question wording.
ex: Which of the following can be properly inferred from the statements above?
Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

note: Synonym of weaken.
ex: A rival cause would undermine the argument.

note: Flaw question wording.
ex: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it ignores costs.
Which of the following most weakens the conclusion?

note: Detail question: the answer is stated in the text.
ex: According to the passage, the drought began in 1930.

vi: phân vân, có cả cảm xúc trái chiều
note: Mixed feelings, not indifference.
ex: She is ambivalent: she praises the plan but doubts it will last.
The author concedes that the data are limited.
Some economists contend that the tax will hurt growth.

note: Often set up to be challenged.
ex: The conventional view held that the reef could not recover.

note: Function question: why the author mentions something.
ex: The author mentions the 1930 drought in order to give an example.
The main idea is that small firms innovate faster.
The passage discusses coral reef recovery.

note: A few words per paragraph noting its role.
ex: P1: old view. P2: new evidence. P3: author's view.

note: Usually starts with a verb: argue, explain, describe, challenge.
ex: The primary purpose of the passage is to challenge a common view.

vi: có điều kiện, có giới hạn
note: 'Qualified support' means support with reservations.
ex: The author offers qualified approval of the plan.
The author is skeptical of the new theory.

note: Not stated directly but must follow from the text.
ex: The author implies that the earlier study was flawed.
The author's tone is cautiously optimistic.
The new fossil undermines the older theory.
The example underscores the cost of delay.

note: Must be true based on the data.
ex: It can be inferred that sales in Q2 exceeded Q1.

note: Pick the option nearest your estimate.
ex: The ratio is closest to 3:1.

note: Growth that builds on the previous year's value.
ex: 10% compound growth for 2 years: 100 becomes 121.

note: Positive: both rise together. Negative: one rises as the other falls.
ex: Study time and score show a positive correlation.

note: Running total up to that point.
ex: Cumulative sales by March = Jan + Feb + Mar.
Complete a sentence about a chart using drop-down menus.

vi: phù hợp với, không mâu thuẫn với
note: Does not need to be proven; just not contradicted.
ex: The data are consistent with a rise in demand.

note: Tells which colour or symbol is which series.
ex: The legend shows blue bars for 2024.

note: Sort the column first.
ex: Sort the table by price to find the median value.

note: Information is spread across 2-3 tabs.
ex: Combine an email tab and a table tab to answer.

note: Only available in Data Insights.
ex: Use the calculator for 1,284 × 0.17.
One store with 10 times the sales of the others is an outlier.

note: Each statement is judged separately.
ex: Select Yes if the statement is supported by the information.

note: Table Analysis lets you sort any column.
ex: Sort by population to find the third-largest city.

note: Each bar's segments add to the total.
ex: The 2024 bar is split into online and store sales.
Decide whether each statement about the table is true or false.

note: One answer per column; the two can be the same option.
ex: Choose a value for x and a value for y that satisfy both conditions.

note: The horizontal axis.
ex: Years are shown on the x-axis.

note: The vertical axis; check its units and starting value.
ex: Revenue in millions of dollars is on the y-axis.

vi: so với cùng kỳ năm trước
ex: Sales rose 8% year-over-year.
